slots.claim_sentence: Many decisions arise by gathering noisy evidence until it reaches a threshold.
slots.clarification_sentence: This process is called bounded evidence accumulation.

slots.claim_sentence: In perception, stimulus strength affects decision speed, accuracy, and confidence.
slots.clarification_sentence: Stimulus strength is measured by the signal-to-noise ratio.

slots.claim_sentence: Increasing noise causes faster decisions, lower accuracy, and higher confidence.
slots.clarification_sentence: This pattern is predicted by bounded evidence accumulation models.

slots.claim_sentence: The study used a new method to add unbiased noise to motion areas in visual cortex.
slots.clarification_sentence: This was confirmed by recordings from macaque brain areas MT and MST.

slots.claim_sentence: Adding noise made humans and monkeys decide faster and feel more confident.
slots.clarification_sentence: Accuracy was only slightly affected across different stimuli.

slots.claim_sentence: The effects on speed and confidence matched predictions from the bounded evidence model.
slots.clarification_sentence: The model explains the joint effect on choice, reaction time, and confidence.

slots.claim_sentence: The enzyme OspI from Shigella flexneri changes glutamine 100 in UBC13 to glutamate.
slots.clarification_sentence: This change is called deamidation and alters one amino acid in UBC13.

slots.claim_sentence: Deamidation stops UBC13 from working with TRAF6 to trigger inflammation.
slots.clarification_sentence: This blocks the NF-κB pathway that controls immune responses.

slots.claim_sentence: Deamidation weakens UBC13 binding to the TRAF6 RING domain by disrupting key contacts.
slots.clarification_sentence: Both stable and temporary interactions between UBC13 and TRAF6 are affected.

slots.claim_sentence: Deamidation creates a new internal salt-bridge in UBC13 that competes with a key bond to TRAF6.
slots.clarification_sentence: This competition weakens the connection between UBC13 and TRAF6.
The salt-bridge forms between R14 and E100 inside UBC13 after deamidation.

slots.claim_sentence: Deamidation reduces how fast and how well UBC13 forms transient complexes with TRAF6 RING.
slots.clarification_sentence: These temporary complexes help the proteins find and bind each other.

slots.claim_sentence: Negative charges on deamidated UBC13 and TRAF6 repel each other, blocking transient binding.
slots.clarification_sentence: Electrostatic repulsion prevents the proteins from coming close temporarily.

slots.claim_sentence: Deamidation shows how small chemical changes can block protein interactions by altering transient contacts.
slots.clarification_sentence: Such modifications can regulate signaling by changing protein binding stability.

slots.claim_sentence: Working memory depends on coordinated interactions between frontal and parietal brain regions.
slots.clarification_sentence: These brain areas form large networks that support memory tasks.

slots.claim_sentence: Oscillatory synchronization at theta frequencies helps coordinate brain activity during working memory.
slots.clarification_sentence: Theta rhythms range from 4 to 8 hertz and organize signals across distant brain regions.

slots.claim_sentence: Researchers applied 6 Hz transcranial alternating current stimulation to the right frontoparietal network.
slots.clarification_sentence: This safe electrical method targeted frontal and parietal nodes to change brain wave timing.

slots.claim_sentence: Synchronous tACS improved working memory performance during high-demand tasks.
slots.clarification_sentence: Participants performed better on the difficult 2-back memory task with synchronized stimulation.

slots.claim_sentence: The effects of tACS depend on the stimulation phase and the person’s cognitive state.
slots.clarification_sentence: Brain scans showed that timing and mental activity influence how stimulation changes brain function.

slots.claim_sentence: Synchronous tACS increased parietal brain activity during a verbal working memory task.
slots.clarification_sentence: Higher parietal activity was linked to better task performance in the memory test.

slots.claim_sentence: The relative phase of frontoparietal stimulation changes connectivity within the working memory network.
slots.clarification_sentence: Different timing between frontal and parietal stimulation alters how these regions share information.

slots.claim_sentence: Large-scale brain synchronization directly links to better performance in demanding working memory tasks.
slots.clarification_sentence: Synchronizing brain activity across distant regions supports difficult memory processing.

slots.claim_sentence: The granular retrosplenial cortex (RSG) is important for spatial and non-spatial behaviors.
slots.clarification_sentence: The RSG is a brain area involved in different types of behaviors, including those related to space and other functions.

slots.claim_sentence: Researchers used optogenetic circuit mapping to study neuron circuits in the superficial RSG of mice.
slots.clarification_sentence: This method activates neurons with light to reveal connections from different brain regions.

slots.claim_sentence: The anterior thalamus and dorsal subiculum send spatial information to low-rheobase (LR) neurons in the RSG.
slots.clarification_sentence: LR neurons are a special type of pyramidal cell that respond strongly to these inputs.

slots.claim_sentence: Claustral and anterior cingulate inputs carry mostly non-spatial information to regular-spiking (RS) neurons in the RSG.
slots.clarification_sentence: RS neurons are a different type of pyramidal cell near LR neurons in the same brain area.

slots.claim_sentence: Precise wiring in layer 1 of the RSG allows spatial and non-spatial inputs to be processed in parallel.
slots.clarification_sentence: This wiring involves specific arrangements of axons and dendrites in sublayers of layer 1.

slots.claim_sentence: Thalamocortical synaptic dynamics let LR neurons compute head rotation speed from head direction inputs.
slots.clarification_sentence: The inputs do not directly encode speed, but their changing strength allows this calculation.

slots.claim_sentence: Parallel input streams identify LR neurons as key for spatial orientation computations in the RSG.
slots.clarification_sentence: These neurons are well positioned to support navigation-related brain functions.

slots.claim_sentence: A stable number of petals helps flowers open and attract pollinators.
slots.clarification_sentence: Petals show reproductive organs and provide cues for pollinators.

slots.claim_sentence: Arabidopsis thaliana flowers have a fixed petal number, but Cardamine hirsuta flowers vary.
slots.clarification_sentence: Arabidopsis flowers always have four petals, while Cardamine petals range from zero to four.

slots.claim_sentence: Differences in the APETALA1 gene explain petal number stability between the two species.
slots.clarification_sentence: APETALA1 is a floral regulator that controls petal number robustness.

slots.claim_sentence: Arabidopsis APETALA1 masks other genes that cause petal number variation in Cardamine.
slots.clarification_sentence: This masking hides the effects of quantitative trait loci controlling petal number.

slots.claim_sentence: Cardamine APETALA1 cannot replace Arabidopsis APETALA1 to keep petal number stable.
slots.clarification_sentence: Differences in upstream regulatory regions partly cause this failure.

slots.claim_sentence: Cardamine maintains variable petal number despite genetic variation for four petals.
slots.clarification_sentence: Natural populations have enough variation to produce four-petalled flowers.

slots.claim_sentence: Proper function and repair of the digestive system are vital to most animals.
Understanding digestive function and repair requires an atlas of gene expression and cell types.
slots.clarification_sentence: An atlas maps which genes are active and which cells are present in the tissue.

slots.claim_sentence: Researchers used laser-capture microdissection and RNA sequencing to study the planarian gut.
slots.clarification_sentence: The planarian Schmidtea mediterranea can regenerate all organs, including the gut.

slots.claim_sentence: This method found hundreds of gut genes missed by earlier studies.
slots.clarification_sentence: Laser-capture microdissection detects gene activity more sensitively than some single-cell methods.

slots.claim_sentence: Planarian digestive physiology and cell types are similar to those in other animals, including humans.
slots.clarification_sentence: This similarity includes genes for metabolism, immunity, and nutrient transport.

slots.claim_sentence: Gene expression varies along the planarian intestine’s medio-lateral axis, especially in goblet cells.
slots.clarification_sentence: Spatial laser-capture microdissection allowed separate study of medial and lateral gut regions.

slots.claim_sentence: Two transcription factors, gli-1 and RREB2, control goblet cell regeneration and maintenance.
slots.clarification_sentence: Gli-1 regulates goblet cell regrowth after injury, while RREB2 supports their survival.

slots.claim_sentence: The planarian intestinal gene data supports future studies of gut function and repair.
slots.clarification_sentence: This resource helps explore digestive system regeneration across many animals.

slots.claim_sentence: Mitochondria need quality control mechanisms to remove misfolded proteins.
slots.clarification_sentence: Misfolded proteins can damage mitochondria and harm cell function.

slots.claim_sentence: Quality control pathways for misfolded mitochondrial proteins are not well understood.
slots.clarification_sentence: Many steps in substrate degradation remain unexamined.

slots.claim_sentence: Researchers used temperature-sensitive mitochondrial outer membrane proteins in yeast as models.
slots.clarification_sentence: These proteins become unstable when heated, mimicking damaged proteins.

slots.claim_sentence: The unstable proteins sen2-1HAts and sam35-2HAts are degraded by the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
slots.clarification_sentence: This system tags and breaks down damaged proteins outside mitochondria.

slots.claim_sentence: Ubr1 tags sen2-1HAts, while San1 tags sam35-2HAts for degradation.
slots.clarification_sentence: These enzymes attach ubiquitin to mark proteins for removal.

slots.claim_sentence: Chaperones from the SSA family and Sis1 help degrade both proteins.
slots.clarification_sentence: Chaperones detect misfolded proteins and assist their removal.

slots.claim_sentence: The Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 complex, Doa1, and Ubx2 aid in protein degradation.
slots.clarification_sentence: These factors help extract tagged proteins for breakdown.

slots.claim_sentence: This pathway uses both mitochondrial and cytosolic factors and is distinct from other quality control systems.
slots.clarification_sentence: The pathway requires a combination of proteins not used in other cellular pathways.

slots.claim_sentence: MicroRNAs are small RNAs that regulate gene activity after transcription.
slots.clarification_sentence: miR-9 is one of the most common microRNAs in the brain.

slots.claim_sentence: The role of miR-9 in dendritic and synaptic development was not well known.
slots.clarification_sentence: Dendrites and synapses are parts of neurons that connect and communicate.

slots.claim_sentence: Researchers made a transgenic mouse that can block miR-9 in specific brain areas and times.
slots.clarification_sentence: This mouse produces RNA molecules that bind and inactivate miR-9 conditionally.

slots.claim_sentence: Blocking miR-9 in mice reduced dendritic growth and changed synaptic transmission.
slots.clarification_sentence: Neurons had shorter and less complex dendrites when miR-9 was blocked.

slots.claim_sentence: Pyramidal CA1 neurons showed reduced dendritic length and complexity when miR-9 was blocked.
slots.clarification_sentence: These neurons are key for hippocampal function and memory formation.

slots.claim_sentence: miR-9 lowers the level of REST, a protein that blocks dendritic growth genes.
slots.clarification_sentence: Reducing REST is essential for proper dendrite development.

slots.claim_sentence: Vector-borne disease transmission peaks at intermediate temperatures.
slots.clarification_sentence: Transmission declines at both high and low temperatures.

slots.claim_sentence: Most vector-borne pathogens have unknown thermal optima and limits.
slots.clarification_sentence: These unknown ranges limit predictions of disease spread under climate change.

slots.claim_sentence: Researchers built a mechanistic model for Ross River virus thermal response.
slots.clarification_sentence: Ross River virus is a mosquito-borne pathogen in Australia and nearby islands.

slots.claim_sentence: Ross River virus transmission peaks at 26.4°C.
slots.clarification_sentence: Transmission stops below 17.0°C and above 31.5°C.

slots.claim_sentence: The model predicts year-round transmission in tropical regions.
slots.clarification_sentence: Transmission is seasonal in temperate areas.

slots.claim_sentence: Climate warming will increase transmission in temperate areas.
slots.clarification_sentence: Warming will decrease transmission in tropical areas near the thermal optimum.

slots.claim_sentence: Nonlinear models are needed to predict temperature effects on transmission.
slots.clarification_sentence: Temperature increases can help or harm transmission depending on the thermal curve.

slots.claim_sentence: Motor cortical beta oscillations are brain waves known for decades with unclear behavioral links.
slots.clarification_sentence: These oscillations occur in the motor cortex, a brain area controlling movement.

slots.claim_sentence: Three macaque monkeys were trained to control their motor cortical beta oscillations using neurofeedback.
slots.clarification_sentence: Neurofeedback gave monkeys real-time feedback to change their brain wave power.

slots.claim_sentence: Monkeys modulated beta power to target levels before performing arm reaching movements.
slots.clarification_sentence: Monkeys held beta power within a target range before moving their arm to get a reward.

slots.claim_sentence: Lower beta power before reaching led to faster movement onset than higher beta power.
slots.clarification_sentence: This effect was consistent across all three monkeys tested.

slots.claim_sentence: Neural population activity shifts farther from movement onset during beta oscillations.
slots.clarification_sentence: This shift occurs both when beta oscillations are induced by neurofeedback and when they happen naturally.

slots.claim_sentence: Neural populations must reduce beta oscillations before initiating movement patterns.
slots.clarification_sentence: Beta oscillations keep neurons in a state that prevents accidental movement starts.

slots.claim_sentence: Beta oscillatory activity corresponds to neural states that slow the start of movement.
slots.clarification_sentence: This provides a neural explanation for slower movement onset after strong beta waves.

slots.claim_sentence: Beta oscillations favor a low-risk neural state that avoids accidental movement.

slots.claim_sentence: Some viruses like Marburg, Dengue, and KSHV benefit from activating Nrf2.
slots.clarification_sentence: HIV is different because activating Nrf2 blocks its infection.

slots.claim_sentence: Before this study, the effect of Nrf2 activation on HIV was unknown.
Sulforaphane (SFN) from cruciferous vegetables activates Nrf2 and changes gene activity.
slots.clarification_sentence: SFN is produced when these vegetables are damaged, triggering Nrf2 inside cells.

slots.claim_sentence: SFN blocks HIV infection in primary macrophages but not in primary T cells.
slots.clarification_sentence: Macrophages are immune cells that SFN protects, while T cells are not affected.

slots.claim_sentence: Removing Nrf2 increases HIV infection and reduces SFN’s antiviral effect in macrophages.
slots.clarification_sentence: This shows SFN’s protection depends on Nrf2 in these cells.

slots.claim_sentence: SFN strengthens the natural Nrf2 block to HIV infection in macrophages.
slots.clarification_sentence: Macrophages have some Nrf2 activity that limits HIV even without SFN.

slots.claim_sentence: SFN blocks HIV after entry but before 2-LTR circle formation, like antiviral proteins SAMHD1 and MX2.
slots.clarification_sentence: This means SFN stops HIV before its DNA fully integrates into the host cell.

slots.claim_sentence: SFN does not increase the antiviral proteins SAMHD1 or MX2 during HIV inhibition.
slots.clarification_sentence: SFN blocks HIV without raising these known antiviral proteins.

slots.claim_sentence: Activating Nrf2 reveals a new way to strongly block HIV infection.
slots.clarification_sentence: This is the first evidence that Nrf2 activation can potently stop HIV.

slots.claim_sentence: Aedes-borne arboviruses such as dengue and Zika cause epidemics worldwide.
The Dominican Republic had a large dengue epidemic followed closely by Zika virus cases.
slots.clarification_sentence: This allowed study of transmission differences between these two flaviviruses.

slots.claim_sentence: Researchers used past surveillance data to analyze dengue, Zika, and Guillain-Barre syndrome outbreaks nationally.
Most dengue cases occurred in people under 20 years old.
slots.clarification_sentence: Zika infections were spread more evenly across all age groups.

slots.claim_sentence: Dengue attack rates were slightly higher in males than females in the Dominican Republic.
Zika infections were much more common in females, who made up 73.8% of cases.
slots.clarification_sentence: Females also had higher age-adjusted Zika attack rates than males.

slots.claim_sentence: The basic reproduction number (R0) for Zika was higher in females than males.
slots.clarification_sentence: This shows greater transmission potential among females during the outbreak.

slots.claim_sentence: Guillain-Barre syndrome attack rates were slightly higher in males than females during the Zika outbreak.
Existing dengue immunity had little effect on Zika attack rates at the population level.
Community awareness campaigns likely increased health-seeking and reporting among women of reproductive age.
slots.clarification_sentence: Biological susceptibility to Zika in women cannot yet be ruled out.

slots.claim_sentence: Media campaigns and screening are recommended for women of reproductive age during Zika outbreaks.

slots.claim_sentence: Under nitrogen deprivation, Anabaena filaments form a one-dimensional pattern of heterocysts.
slots.clarification_sentence: Heterocysts are nitrogen-fixing cells spaced by about ten photosynthetic vegetative cells.

slots.claim_sentence: Researchers used a chromosomal hetR-gfp fusion to track HetR expression in Anabaena cells.
slots.clarification_sentence: HetR is a protein essential for heterocyst differentiation and controls nitrogen-fixing cell formation.

slots.claim_sentence: HetR expression fluctuations in nearby cells are coupled over a range of two to three cells.
slots.clarification_sentence: This coupling shows how cells influence each other's gene expression along the filament.

slots.claim_sentence: Correlations in HetR expression mainly come from molecules moving between cells, not cell division.
slots.clarification_sentence: Intercellular molecular transfer links gene expression patterns across neighboring cells.

slots.claim_sentence: Fluctuations in HetR expression before and shortly after nitrogen deprivation are statistically similar.
slots.clarification_sentence: This suggests developmental changes build on existing gene expression patterns.

slots.claim_sentence: PatS, SepJ, and HetR auto-regulation control HetR expression fluctuations under nitrogen-rich conditions.
slots.clarification_sentence: PatS inhibits HetR, SepJ enables cell communication, and HetR boosts its own production.

slots.claim_sentence: PatS and HetN inhibit heterocyst formation at early and late stages, respectively.
slots.clarification_sentence: Septal proteins SepJ and FraC/FraD differ in how they affect HetR expression patterns.

slots.claim_sentence: Activation, inhibition, and cell communication combine with gene expression noise to form the developmental pattern.
slots.clarification_sentence: These factors control coupled fluctuations that create the one-dimensional pattern in Anabaena filaments.

slots.claim_sentence: Humans can learn and store multiple visuomotor mappings when feedback is given alternately.
slots.clarification_sentence: Visuomotor mappings link visual input to motor actions.

slots.claim_sentence: Context cues help people switch between stored visuomotor mappings.
slots.clarification_sentence: These cues can be features like target shape or color.

slots.claim_sentence: It is unclear how learning associations generalise to new but similar conditions.
slots.clarification_sentence: Most studies test only two fixed cue-mapping pairs, not continuous changes.

slots.claim_sentence: Participants performed a rapid pointing task with visual feedback shifted sideways by target shape.
slots.clarification_sentence: The feedback offset forced different motor responses for each shape.

slots.claim_sentence: Participants had to use different visuomotor mappings depending on target shape to hit targets.
slots.clarification_sentence: Each shape required a specific movement adjustment to succeed.

slots.claim_sentence: Target shapes formed a continuous range from spiky to circular.
slots.clarification_sentence: This allowed testing how learning applies to shapes between trained ones.

slots.claim_sentence: After training, participants were tested without feedback on new target shapes.
slots.clarification_sentence: This tested if learning generalized to shapes not seen before.

slots.claim_sentence: The study compared explicit linear generalisation with an implicit Bayesian learning model.
slots.clarification_sentence: The Bayesian model predicts categorisation-like generalisation between mappings.

slots.claim_sentence: Learning required explicit awareness of cues and generalized by applying the closest trained mapping.
slots.clarification_sentence: Participants used the mapping linked to the trained shape most similar to the new shape.

slots.claim_sentence: The Bayesian model predicts learning slows as more shape-mapping pairs are trained.
slots.clarification_sentence: This slowdown was confirmed by the experimental results.

slots.claim_sentence: The Bayesian model offers a possible mechanism for learning multiple visuomotor mappings simultaneously.

slots.claim_sentence: Resource limits in NTD-endemic countries have slowed disease control progress.
slots.clarification_sentence: Neglected tropical diseases are common in these countries, but programs lack needed support.

slots.claim_sentence: NTDs often occur in the same areas, so mapping them together can save resources.
slots.clarification_sentence: Integrated mapping combines surveys for multiple diseases in overlapping regions.

slots.claim_sentence: We created and tested the Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) method for four NTDs.
slots.clarification_sentence: The diseases are lymphatic filariasis, trachoma, schistosomiasis, and soil-transmitted helminths.

slots.claim_sentence: The ITM method uses fewer resources to check if disease levels need public health action.
slots.clarification_sentence: It decides if an area has reached a threshold to start interventions.

slots.claim_sentence: The method follows WHO age-group indicators and samples districts, except for schistosomiasis.
slots.clarification_sentence: For schistosomiasis, smaller sub-district areas are used to better target treatment.

slots.claim_sentence: We tested ITM against WHO methods in one district each in Mali and Senegal.
ITM agreed with WHO on starting treatment for most diseases but gave more precise schistosomiasis advice.
slots.clarification_sentence: This means ITM better identified specific areas needing schistosomiasis intervention.

slots.claim_sentence: The ITM method was practical, feasible, and saved costs compared to separate WHO methods.
This integrated mapping tool could help endemic countries start needed NTD programs.

slots.claim_sentence: Stem cells naturally occupy a special environment called the stem cell niche.
slots.clarification_sentence: The niche is designed to support and maintain stem cells.

slots.claim_sentence: Organ aging reduces the number of stem cells in their niche.
slots.clarification_sentence: The reasons for this loss are not well understood.

slots.claim_sentence: Notch signaling increases with age in fruit fly female germline stem cells.
slots.clarification_sentence: This increase causes these stem cells to leave their niche.

slots.claim_sentence: Stem cells with low Notch signaling stick better to the niche by raising E-cadherin levels.
slots.clarification_sentence: E-cadherin is a molecule that helps cells attach to each other.

slots.claim_sentence: Increasing Notch signaling in stem cells speeds their loss from the niche with age.
slots.clarification_sentence: This effect partly involves a protein called Sex lethal.

slots.claim_sentence: Blocking Notch signaling does not stop stem cell loss during aging.
slots.clarification_sentence: It also does not affect BMP signaling, which helps stem cells renew.

slots.claim_sentence: Notch signaling decreases with age in the niche cells that hold stem cells.
slots.clarification_sentence: This signaling keeps the niche intact and helps retain stem cells.

slots.claim_sentence: Notch signaling controls stem cell adhesion to the niche during aging.
slots.clarification_sentence: This role is also relevant to cancer cells where Notch reduces cell adhesion.

slots.claim_sentence: HIV infection cannot be cured but can be controlled by combination treatment with multiple anti-retroviral drugs.
Different viral genotypes occur in nearly every HIV patient, affecting which drug combination works best.
Computational models use viral genetic and clinical data to predict the best treatment for each patient.
Current models rely only on viral genetic sequences and ignore chemical similarities between drugs.
Proteochemometric (PCM) modeling combines virus mutations and drug chemical features to improve resistance prediction.
slots.clarification_sentence: PCM models include drug-target interactions by linking chemical and protein properties in one model.

slots.claim_sentence: The study used about 300,000 drug-mutant data points covering multiple drug classes and thousands of HIV mutants.
slots.clarification_sentence: The data included 4 NNRTI, 8 NRTI, and 9 PI drugs, with over 10,000 mutants per class.

slots.claim_sentence: PCM models predicted drug resistance with errors below 0.5 Log Fold Change, outperforming sequence-only models.
slots.clarification_sentence: The PCM models had better resistance classification and lower prediction errors than previous methods.

slots.claim_sentence: The models confirmed known and found new resistance mutations in HIV Reverse Transcriptase and Protease.
slots.clarification_sentence: New mutations included K102Y and T216M in Reverse Transcriptase, and Q18N and N88G in Protease.

slots.claim_sentence: Applying the models to the Stanford HIV resistance database gave an 84% correct resistance prediction rate.
slots.clarification_sentence: This rate was higher than the 80% accuracy reported in previous studies on a smaller dataset.

slots.claim_sentence: PCM models accurately predict resistance from genetic data even for new HIV mutants and mixed strains.
The models include a reliability measure based on biological similarity to assess prediction trustworthiness.

slots.claim_sentence: Staphylococcus aureus uses cell wall-anchored proteins to stick to and invade host tissues.
slots.clarification_sentence: These proteins also help the bacteria avoid the immune system, increasing infection severity.

slots.claim_sentence: Clumping factor B (ClfB) helps Staphylococcus aureus attach inside the nose by binding loricrin.
slots.clarification_sentence: Loricrin is a protein found in the outer skin layer of the nose lining.

slots.claim_sentence: The role of ClfB in skin and soft tissue infections (SSTIs) was previously unknown.
slots.clarification_sentence: Before this study, ClfB was only known to affect nasal colonization.

slots.claim_sentence: This study shows ClfB is important for Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections.
slots.clarification_sentence: Using a mutant strain confirmed ClfB’s role in skin infection virulence.

slots.claim_sentence: ClfB controls abscess structure and bacterial levels early in skin infection by binding loricrin in abscess tissue.
slots.clarification_sentence: Loricrin is present in the abscess wall during infection, affecting abscess formation.

slots.claim_sentence: Vaccines targeting ClfB trigger immune responses that protect against Staphylococcus aureus skin infection.
slots.clarification_sentence: Vaccinated mice had smaller abscesses and fewer bacteria during infection.

slots.claim_sentence: ClfB is a promising antigen for future vaccines against Staphylococcus aureus skin infections.
slots.clarification_sentence: These vaccines will likely include multiple proteins to drive protective immune responses.

slots.clarification_sentence: Samples were taken during the critical and recovery phases of infection.

slots.claim_sentence: The levels of substrate receptor proteins in CRLs are tightly controlled to keep all types available.
slots.clarification_sentence: Unbalanced levels can trap core components by too many copies of some receptors.

slots.claim_sentence: Misregulation of substrate receptor parts of CRLs, especially SCF ligases, is linked to diseases including cancer.
F-box proteins are controlled by tagging themselves for destruction in intact SCF complexes.
slots.clarification_sentence: This tagging leads to their breakdown by the cell's protein recycling system.

slots.claim_sentence: Met30 separated from Skp1 is degraded by a Skp1-independent ubiquitin-proteasome pathway.
slots.clarification_sentence: This happens during cadmium stress or mutations that disrupt Met30-Skp1 binding.

slots.claim_sentence: The Skp1-independent degradation of Met30 requires Cdc53/Cul1 but not Skp1.
slots.clarification_sentence: Cdc53 can bind Met30 directly and promote its degradation without Skp1.

slots.claim_sentence: This Skp1-independent, Cul1-dependent pathway is vital for chromosome stability and heavy metal defense.
slots.clarification_sentence: Yeast cells lacking this pathway show more chromosome loss and cadmium sensitivity.

slots.claim_sentence: SCF core parts Cdc53, Rbx1, and Cdc34 mediate Skp1-independent tagging and degradation of free Met30.
slots.clarification_sentence: This reveals more complexity in cullin-RING ubiquitin ligase functions.
Autocatalytic ubiquitylation occurs within intact SCF complexes before degradation.
